chapter_title: Concerning why if a [Nail] is cut the Person shall
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of ¶5

Know that the natural mind of a person is like the external ground of the soul , and the fac ulties and powers belonging to it are like the per ceptions that arise within it. There are varieties of perception and understanding that you will find developing in the natural mind. Some arise , and are renewed , and become established with firm ness. These have not been u prooted entirely . Again, there are other perceptions which , if they are destroyed by fals ity, cannot be restored or grow back . And yet others grow again when challenged , for they are like living kn owledges ro oted in good , which, though cut away, regener ate themselves . And still others occur in the mind which , when destroyed , do not return — resembling dead kn owledges from mere memory , which neither develop nor can ever be renewed . It shall seem fitting to the person according to his ruling love , and what develops within imp urity — that is, within fals ity derived from evil — proceeds from his prop rium. The will that is corru pted by hered itary evil dw ells within the living will that is from the Lord , and these corru pted aff ections within the regener ating mind are in a state of spiritual disorder — not wholly dead , but weak ened and dise ased.

---

* Note on difficult passages: * Several lac unae resist confident translation. The distinction between trees that reg row when cut and those that do not corresponds to the spiritual distinction between perceptions gr ounded in genuine good ( which survive tem ptation and return ) and perceptions held only in external memory without internal root ( which, once fals ity sc atters them, are permanently lost ). The closing image of corrupt flesh dwelling within living flesh corresponds to the co ex istence, during regener ation, of the old hered itary will alongside the new will being formed by the Lord — a state Swedenborg describes as spiritual illness preceding full renewal .
